title: When Safety Overrides Vision: Exploring Dynamics between Vision Influence and Safety Alignment in Vision-Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.18628v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Aligned vision-language models (VLMs) are designed to balance grounded visual reasoning with safe generation behavior. However, we observe a striking phenomenon: under safety-constrained instruction, models frequently abstain from answering questions that remain correctly answerable under default instruction despite receiving identical image-question inputs. This raises a fundamental question: does safety alignment suppress perceptual grounding itself, or does visual evidence remain internally available while generation is redirected toward abstention? In this work, we investigate the internal decoding dynamics underlying safety-induced abstention in aligned VLMs. Across multiple architectures and multimodal benchmarks, we show that abstained generations remain consistently influenced by visual evidence throughout decoding, indicating that perceptual grounding is largely preserved despite refusal behavior. translated_title: 当安全超越视觉：探究视觉语言模型中视觉影响与安全对齐之间的动态关系
translated_abstract: 对齐的视觉语言模型（VLMs）旨在平衡基于视觉的推理与安全生成行为。然而，我们观察到一个显著现象：在安全约束指令下，模型经常拒绝回答在默认指令下仍可正确回答的问题，尽管输入了相同的图像-问题对。这引发了一个根本性问题：安全对齐是否抑制了感知基础本身，还是视觉证据在内部仍然可用，而生成行为被转向了拒绝回答？在这项工作中，我们研究了对齐VLMs中安全诱导拒绝背后的内部解码动态。跨多种架构和多模态基准测试，我们表明，被拒绝的生成在解码过程中始终受到视觉证据的影响，表明尽管存在拒绝行为，感知基础在很大程度上得以保留。我们进一步证明，
tldr: 本文揭示了安全对齐的视觉语言模型在拒绝回答时仍保留视觉感知基础，安全约束主要改变生成方向而非抑制视觉理解。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that safety-aligned vision-language models retain visual perceptual grounding during refusal, with safety constraints primarily redirecting generation rather than suppressing visual understanding.
